text.p: Following are highlights of some of the main stories in Croatian newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Baranja region connected to the Croatian power grid. A double 40-megawatt cable running between Osijek and Bilje will enable an unhindered electricity supply to Baranja.
- Three Croat houses blown up in Moslem-held Bugojno in central Bosnia.
- Croatia prepared to open three border crossings toward the Bosnian Serb entity on September 1.
- Drastic decline on the world bourses: Prices fell on the London, New York, Frankfurt and Hong Kong stock exchanges after the Bundesbank announced a likely interest rate increase.
- Croatian stocks also turn bearish, food processor Podravka ends the week as the biggest loser.
- Representatives of an American Christian-Jewish centre for understanding on a visit to Croatia say they had been receiving one-sided reports about the country.
- Private entrepreneurs earn more and pay less in wages to their employees, according to 1996 results compiled by the central payments bureau.
- Initial results of a workforce survey according to European criteria show 100,000 fewer unemployed people. Workforce figure revised up to 1.54 from 1.43 million.
- The last deadline for reporting arms to the Interior Ministry runs out on August 19.
- Commentary: Talks in Frankfurt between Klaus Kinkel and Mate Granic show Germany is prepared to enforce a more pro-active policy toward Croatia and former Yugoslavia.
- German firms may take part in the restructuring of the Croatian state railway company.
- Istrian opposition party IDS reacts with horror to plans by the electricity board HEP to add a third coal-fired thermo-electric power plant to the Plomin complex. -- Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075
